objective.statement: Read the compound time signatures 6/8, 9/8 and 12/8.
successCriteria: I know the top number counts quavers.
I can find the number of dotted-crotchet beats by dividing the top number by 3.
I can call 6/8, 9/8 and 12/8 compound duple, triple and quadruple.

explanation.text: In 6/8, 9/8 and 12/8 the bottom number is 8, so the top number counts quavers. Three quavers make one dotted-crotchet beat, so you divide the top number by three to find the number of beats.

explanation.caption: 6/8: six quavers, two dotted-crotchet beats. Compound duple.

music.textAlternative: One bar of 12/8 with four dotted crotchets.
music.questionAlternative: Bar 1: dotted crotchet, dotted crotchet, dotted crotchet, dotted crotchet.

explanation.caption: 12/8: twelve quavers, four beats. Compound quadruple.

explanation.text: Do not confuse 6/8 with 3/4. A bar of each is the same length, six quavers. But 3/4 has three crotchet beats that divide into two, and 6/8 has two dotted-crotchet beats that divide into three. The groups of beamed quavers show which one you are reading.
Top number ÷ 3 = number of beats. 6/8 = 2 beats, 9/8 = 3 beats, 12/8 = 4 beats. All three have dotted-crotchet beats.

steps: Group them in threes: two beats, each a group of three quavers.
Two beats, three quavers each: this is compound duple time.
